My day was good.

The child studied well.

text: Omuka oine bintu ki omu nju?
translation_en: What things do you have at home?
I have a table, a book and a chair at home.
Do you have a table and a chair?
Yes, I have a table and a chair.
Now I am using a computer to write.

I am well, sir. Are you well, sir?
I am fine, sir, and you?
I am fine.
Okay, how is the family?
They are fine.
Okay, I want grasshoppers. Do you have grasshoppers?
Do you like grasshoppers?
I like grasshoppers very much!
Okay! I have grasshoppers.

text: Kare, ekikopo ky'ensenene ni shiringi zingahi?
translation_en: Okay, how much is a cup of grasshoppers?
Five thousand.
Okay, do you have baskets?
No, sir.
Okay, do you have chicken and cabbage?

text: Nyine enkoko emwe na zakabegi ishatu.
translation_en: I have one chicken and three cabbages.

text: Nkoko na zakabegi ni shiringi zingahi?
translation_en: How much are the chicken and cabbage?
Twenty thousand.

text: Kale. Oyebare munungo. Osiibegye sebo! Ninza kukureeba nyencakare/nyekyakare.
translation_en: Okay. Thank you very much. Have a good day, sir! I'll see you tomorrow.
Okay, have a good day, sir!
I woke up early this morning.

text: Nkayogya amaisho gangye kandi naayeyogya ekibuga.
translation_en: I washed my face and swept the compound.

text: Bwanyima nkakora kyayi kandi naarya kyamushansa n'eka yangye.
translation_en: Then I made tea and ate breakfast with my family.
It rained heavily last night.

text: Oruguuto orurikuza omu katare rurimu ebyondo eriizooba.
translation_en: The road to the market is muddy today.

text: Ninteekateeka ngu eizooba niriija kurugayo nyenkyakare kugira ngu ebijwaro byome.
translation_en: I hope the sun comes out tomorrow so the clothes can dry.

text: Munyanyowe omuto naaza aha ishomero buri kasheeshe.
translation_en: My younger sister goes to school every morning.

text: Naakunda okubara kwonka naashanga Orungyereza rugumire.
translation_en: She likes mathematics but finds English difficult.

text: Omwegyesa waitu naatuha ekibuuzo eky'okukorera omuka buri izooba.
translation_en: Our teacher gives us homework every day.

text: Taata wangye naahinga ebihimba hamwe na nebitookye omu musiri.
translation_en: My father grows beans and matooke in the garden.

text: Omu siizoni egi enjura etwire eri nungi, nahabwekyo ebihingwa biriyo nibikura kurungi.
translation_en: This season the rain has been good, so the crops are growing well.
We will harvest in two months.

text: Nyomwebazyo nkataayaayira omunywani ou naabaire ntakareebire omu bwire bureingwa.
translation_en: Yesterday I visited a friend I had not seen in a long time.

text: Tukashutama aheeru kandi twagamba kumara eshaaha nyingi.
translation_en: We sat outside and talked for hours.

text: Ntakagyenzire, akampa obucoori obwokyize kugira ngu ngutware omuka.
translation_en: Before I left, she gave me some roasted maize to take home.
He who lacks wisdom pounds in a cooking clay pot. [meaning: Acting without thought or common sense leads to self-destruction or ruining valuable things.]
He who guides you through the dark night is thanked when morning comes. [meaning: You appreciate a person's help or guidance once you safely see the outcome of a difficult situation.]

You feed all the puppies because you do not know which one will hunt best. [meaning: Do not write off any child or person; invest in everyone because you never know who will succeed or help in the future.]

text: Mpora mpora ekahitsya omunyongororwa aha iziba
translation_en: Slowly by slowly, the earthworm reached the well. [meaning: Patience, perseverance, and consistency bring ultimate success, much like 'slow and steady wins the race'.]
One stick at a time makes the bundle. [meaning: Small, consistent efforts or cooperation lead to accomplishing big goals.]
A stick is straightened while it is still young and fresh. [meaning: A person is tamed, taught, or disciplined when they are still young.]

text: Akanyonyi akataragyenda nikagira ngu nyina niwe amanya kuteeka
translation_en: A bird that has never traveled thinks its mother is the only one who knows how to cook. [meaning: Exposure expands your worldview. If you never travel or open your mind to new experiences, you will think your own way of living is the only correct one.]

A woman who was once poor or miserable does not easily forget her past. [meaning: Hard times leave lasting lessons. A person who has truly struggled remains humble, cautious, and deeply appreciative of their success.]

text: Ilé ọba tó jó, ẹwà ló bù sí.
translation_en: Make the best of any tragic or difficult situation; good can come out of adversity.

text: Bí àgbàda ò bá gbóná, àgbàdo ò lèè ta.
translation_en: Good things do not always come easy; hard work and tough times build success (no pain, no gain).

text: Báwo ni ojú ọ̀jọ̀ ṣe rí lónìí?
translation_en: How is the weather today?
